nodes.description: Glottic stenosis and laryngeal webs make intubation difficult or impossible; anesthesia requires planning for a difficult airway, and tracheostomy may be needed emergently.

evidence.reference_title: Delivery of anesthesia and complications for children with Fraser syndrome: a review of 125 anesthetics.
evidence.snippet: One child was a difficult intubation requiring an ID 2.5 mm oral endotracheal tube (ETT), and one child was an impossible intubation that required an emergency tracheostomy to secure the airway.

evidence.reference_title: Delivery of anesthesia and complications for children with Fraser syndrome: a review of 125 anesthetics.
evidence.snippet: There were a total of ten anesthetic complications in the review, all related to management of the airway.

nodes.description: Biallelic, predominantly truncating germline variants in FRAS1 or FREM2 abolish one of the two large basement-membrane extracellular matrix proteins of the FRAS/FREM complex. The blebbed mouse, which carries a premature termination codon in Fras1, lacks Fras1 protein.
nodes.id: Biallelic FRAS1 or FREM2 Loss of Function

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and mouse blebbed phenotype caused by mutations in FRAS1/Fras1 encoding a putative extracellular matrix protein.
evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis identified five frameshift mutations in FRAS1

evidence.reference_title: Fras1 deficiency results in cryptophthalmos, renal agenesis and blebbed phenotype in mice.
evidence.snippet: We show that bl/bl homozygous embryos are devoid of Fras1 protein

evidence.reference_title: Mild recessive mutations in six Fraser syndrome-related genes cause isolated congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract.
evidence.snippet: Our results also indicate that biallelic missense mutations in the Fraser/MOTA/BNAR spectrum genes cause isolated CAKUT, whereas truncating mutations are found in the multiorgan form of Fraser syndrome.

genetic_context.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous frameshift, nonsense and splice variants predominate; missense FREM2 alleles also occur.

nodes.description: Biallelic GRIP1 splice, frameshift or nonsense variants remove the multi-PDZ scaffold GRIP1. The first two PDZ domains of GRIP1 bind the FRAS1 C-terminal tail as a tandem supramodule.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GRIP1 cause Fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: RT-PCR analysis of the GRIP1 mRNA showed that the c.2113+1G→C splice mutation causes skipping of exon 17, leading to a frame shift and a premature stop of translation.

evidence.reference_title: Supramodular nature of GRIP1 revealed by the structure of its PDZ12 tandem in complex with the carboxyl tail of Fras1.
evidence.snippet: The crystal structure of GRIP1 PDZ12 in complex with the Fras1 C-terminal peptide reveals that the PDZ12 tandem forms a supramodule in which only the peptide-binding groove of PDZ1 is bound with the Fras1 peptide.

genetic_context.description: Reported alleles include a donor splice variant (c.2113+1G>C) that skips exon 17, a 4-bp deletion and a nonsense variant.

nodes.description: FRAS1, FREM1 and FREM2 form a secreted ternary complex that is co-stabilized beneath the lamina densa of embryonic epithelial basement membranes. Loss of FRAS1, FREM2 or GRIP1 depletes the whole complex from the basement membrane zone.
nodes.id: Collapse of the FRAS1-FREM1-FREM2 Basement Membrane Complex

evidence.reference_title: Breakdown of the reciprocal stabilization of QBRICK/Frem1, Fras1, and Frem2 at the basement membrane provokes Fraser syndrome-like defects.
evidence.snippet: When expressed and secreted by transfected cells, these proteins formed a ternary complex, raising the possibility that their reciprocal stabilization at the basement membrane is due to complex formation.

evidence.reference_title: The Fras1/Frem family of extracellular matrix proteins: structure, function, and association with Fraser syndrome and the mouse bleb phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Loss of any of these proteins results in the collapse of the protein assembly, thus providing a molecular explanation for the highly similar phenotypic defects displayed by the respective mutant mice.

evidence.reference_title: Basement membrane distortions impair lung lobation and capillary organization in the mouse model for fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Immunogold histochemistry identified Fras1 as a component of the extracellular matrix localized below the lamina densa of epithelial basement membranes in the embryonic lung.

nodes.description: Skin continuous from forehead to cheek covers a partially or fully formed globe (complete), or the upper lid is fused to the cornea (abortive/incomplete). Uni- or bilateral; the most frequent and most characteristic feature, but not obligatory.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and cryptophthalmos: review of the diagnostic criteria and evidence for phenotypic modules in complex malformation syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Cryptophthalmos was present in 103/117 (88%)

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome: features suggestive of prenatal diagnosis in a review of 38 cases.
evidence.snippet: Renal anomalies and syndactyly were present in 37/38 cases, cryptophtalmos in 36/38, airways anomalies in 30/37 and genital anomalies in 30/35 cases.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome without cryptophthalmos: Two cases.
evidence.snippet: Here we report two atypical cases of Fraser syndrome due to mutations in the FRAS1 gene without cryptophthalmos.

nodes.description: Soft-tissue (membranous) syndactyly of fingers and/or toes.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and cryptophthalmos: review of the diagnostic criteria and evidence for phenotypic modules in complex malformation syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Cryptophthalmos was present in 103/117 (88%), syndactyly in 72/117 (61.5%), and ambiguous genitalia in 20/117 (17.1%).

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome: epidemiological study in a European population.
evidence.snippet: Eye anomalies were found in 20/24 (83%), syndactyly in 14/24 (58%), and laryngeal anomalies in 5/24 (21%) patients.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome without cryptophthalmos: Two cases.
evidence.snippet: The second proband had membranous syndactyly of the four extremities

nodes.description: FRAS1 coats the branching ureteric bud. In Fras1-deficient embryos the bud fails to invade the metanephric mesenchyme, which involutes; expression of GDNF and GDF11 in the renal primordia is deficient, and supplying either factor restores bud invasion in organ culture.
nodes.id: Defective Ureteric Bud Invasion of Metanephric Mesenchyme

animal_models.genotype: Fras1 bl/bl (premature termination) or targeted Fras1-/-
animal_models.name: Fras1 blebbed (bl/bl) and Fras1-null mouse
Fras1 bl/bl with Sprouty1 haploinsufficiency (renal rescue)

evidence.reference_title: Fras1, a basement membrane-associated protein mutated in Fraser syndrome, mediates both the initiation of the mammalian kidney and the integrity of renal glomeruli.
evidence.snippet: In vivo, the bl/bl bud fails to invade metanephric mesenchyme which undergoes involution, events replicated in organ culture.

evidence.reference_title: Fras1, a basement membrane-associated protein mutated in Fraser syndrome, mediates both the initiation of the mammalian kidney and the integrity of renal glomeruli.
evidence.snippet: The expression of glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor and growth-differentiation factor 11 was defective in bl/bl renal primordia in vivo, whereas, in culture, the addition of either growth factor restored bud invasion into the mesenchyme.

evidence.reference_title: Sprouty1 haploinsufficiency prevents renal agenesis in a model of Fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The metanephric mesenchyme of these mutants fails to express sufficient Gdnf, which activates receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signalling, contributing to the phenotype.

nodes.description: Without the FRAS/FREM complex the embryonic epidermis loses its adhesion to the underlying dermis, forming serous and later hemorrhagic subepidermal blisters ("blebs"). In the mouse these blisters precede fused eyelids and digits.

animal_models.genotype: Fras1 bl/bl (premature termination) or targeted Fras1-/-
animal_models.name: Fras1 blebbed (bl/bl) and Fras1-null mouse

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a new gene mutated in Fraser syndrome and mouse myelencephalic blebs.
evidence.snippet: Fras1 mutant mice have a blebbed phenotype characterized by intrauterine epithelial fragility generating serous and, later, hemorrhagic blisters.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and mouse blebbed phenotype caused by mutations in FRAS1/Fras1 encoding a putative extracellular matrix protein.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the bl mouse is a model for Fraser syndrome in humans, a disorder caused by disrupted epithelial integrity in utero.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and mouse blebbed phenotype caused by mutations in FRAS1/Fras1 encoding a putative extracellular matrix protein.
evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis identified five frameshift mutations in FRAS1

evidence.reference_title: Congenital High Airway Obstruction Syndrome (CHAOS) as part of Fraser syndrome: ultrasound and autopsy findings.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis was confirmed by mutation analysis of FRAS1.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a new gene mutated in Fraser syndrome and mouse myelencephalic blebs.
evidence.snippet: Two individuals with Fraser syndrome were homozygous with respect to the same missense mutation of FREM2, confirming genetic heterogeneity.

nodes.description: Without GRIP1, FRAS1 is not delivered to the basal side of embryonic epithelial cells and so is not deposited into the basement membrane.

animal_models.genotype: Grip1 eb/eb (deletion of two coding exons) or targeted Grip1-/-
animal_models.name: Grip1 eye-blebs (eb) and Grip1-null mouse

evidence.reference_title: A direct functional link between the multi-PDZ domain protein GRIP1 and the Fraser syndrome protein Fras1.
evidence.snippet: GRIP1 can physically interact with Fras1 and is required for the localization of Fras1 to the basal side of cells.

nodes.description: Experimental fetal intervention: percutaneous fetoscopic and ultrasound-guided tracheal decompression in a hydropic fetus with laryngeal atresia, followed by EXIT delivery. A single case report; not an established therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Fetoscopic and ultrasound-guided decompression of the fetal trachea in a human fetus with Fraser syndrome and congenital high airway obstruction syndrome (CHAOS) from laryngeal atresia.
evidence.snippet: Abnormal fetoplacental blood flow normalized within hours as a result of the intervention.

evidence.reference_title: Fetoscopic and ultrasound-guided decompression of the fetal trachea in a human fetus with Fraser syndrome and congenital high airway obstruction syndrome (CHAOS) from laryngeal atresia.
evidence.snippet: Weaning from ventilation was achieved at 18 days of postnatal life.

nodes.description: Reducing the ureteric bud's Sprouty1 dose enhances receptor tyrosine kinase signalling and prevents renal agenesis in blebbed mice; exogenous FGF10 rescues mutant rudiments in vitro.
nodes.id: Fras1 bl/bl with Sprouty1 haploinsufficiency (renal rescue)

evidence.reference_title: Sprouty1 haploinsufficiency prevents renal agenesis in a model of Fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We found that fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling contributed to this genetic rescue, and exogenous FGF10 rescued defects in Fras1(bl/bl) rudiments in vitro.

nodes.description: Fras1-deficient embryos develop subepidermal hemorrhagic blisters, fused eyelids and digits, and unilateral or bilateral renal agenesis; on a C57BL6J background renal agenesis is consistent, whereas some mutants on mixed backgrounds survive with two kidneys.

evidence.reference_title: Fras1 deficiency results in cryptophthalmos, renal agenesis and blebbed phenotype in mice.
evidence.snippet: The defects observed in Fras1-/- mice phenocopy those of the existing bl (blebbed) mouse mutants, which have been considered a model for the human genetic disorder Fraser syndrome.

nodes.description: Bleb mutant mapped to Frem2; Frem2 loss depletes Fras1 and Frem1 from the basement membrane, and surviving adults develop renal cysts.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a new gene mutated in Fraser syndrome and mouse myelencephalic blebs.
evidence.snippet: We mapped my to Frem2, a gene related to Fras1 and Frem1, and showed that a Frem2 gene-trap mutation was allelic to my.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GRIP1 cause Fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in GRIP1 cause classic FS in humans.

evidence.reference_title: The first adolescent case of Fraser syndrome 3, with a novel nonsense variant in GRIP1.
evidence.snippet: We present a 15.5-year old Pakistani boy with homozygous truncating variant c.1774C>T (p.Gln592Ter).

nodes.description: Grip1 loss produces subepidermal hemorrhagic blisters, renal agenesis, syndactyly or polydactyly and cryptophthalmos, with failure of Fras1 localization to the basal cell side.

evidence.reference_title: A direct functional link between the multi-PDZ domain protein GRIP1 and the Fraser syndrome protein Fras1.
evidence.snippet: In one animal model of Fraser syndrome, the eye-blebs (eb) mouse, Grip1 is disrupted by a deletion of two coding exons.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome: features suggestive of prenatal diagnosis in a review of 38 cases.
evidence.snippet: detectable anomalies included oligohydramnios (22), ascites/hydrops (9), renal anomalies (20)

nodes.description: Review-level synthesis attributes the malformations of Fraser syndrome to disturbed epithelial-mesenchymal interactions during embryogenesis. Unlike the epidermal and renal steps, organ-specific mechanisms for the laryngeal, genital, anorectal, auricular, nasal and other malformations have not been demonstrated, so this node is not linked to individual phenotypes (see the knowledge-gap discussion).

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome: review of the literature illustrated by a historical adult case.
evidence.snippet: The syndrome is related to mutations in three different genes (FRAS1, FREM2, and GRIP1) resulting in failure of the apoptosis program and disruption of the epithelial-mesenchymal interactions during embryonic development.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in GRIP1 cause Fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Both FRAS1 and FREM2 encode extracellular matrix proteins that are essential for the adhesion between epidermal basement membrane and the underlying dermal connective tissues during embryonic development.

nodes.description: In Fras1-null mouse embryos, pulmonary lobes fail to separate and terminal air-sac capillaries are disorganized. A corresponding human lung phenotype has not been systematically characterized.
nodes.id: Impaired Pulmonary Lobe Septation and Capillary Organization

evidence.reference_title: Basement membrane distortions impair lung lobation and capillary organization in the mouse model for fraser syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Embryos homozygous for a targeted mutation of Fras1 exhibited fused pulmonary lobes resulting from incomplete separation during development as well as a profound disarrangement of blood capillaries in the terminal air sacs.

nodes.description: Complete laryngeal obstruction, prenatally presenting as congenital high airway obstruction syndrome (CHAOS) with enlarged echogenic lungs and hydrops. No frequency is assigned: a 38-case fetal series reports "airways anomalies" in 30/37, a broader category that also covers laryngeal stenosis and webs and does not separate atresia.

evidence.reference_title: Fetoscopic and ultrasound-guided decompression of the fetal trachea in a human fetus with Fraser syndrome and congenital high airway obstruction syndrome (CHAOS) from laryngeal atresia.
evidence.snippet: We attempted percutaneous fetoscopic and ultrasound-guided tracheal decompression in a hydropic human fetus with CHAOS associated with Fraser syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital High Airway Obstruction Syndrome (CHAOS) as part of Fraser syndrome: ultrasound and autopsy findings.
evidence.snippet: We describe a case report of CHAOS, with additional malformations diagnosed at 20 weeks.

nodes.description: Glottic or subglottic narrowing, a cause of difficult or impossible intubation and of emergency tracheostomy.

evidence.reference_title: Delivery of anesthesia and complications for children with Fraser syndrome: a review of 125 anesthetics.
evidence.snippet: there is a relatively high incidence of difficult or impossible tracheal intubation (20%) due to glottic stenosis

nodes.description: Unilateral or bilateral absence of the kidney; bilateral agenesis is lethal and is a leading cause of prenatal detection.

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome and cryptophthalmos: review of the diagnostic criteria and evidence for phenotypic modules in complex malformation syndromes.
evidence.snippet: renal agenesis in 53/117 (45.3%)

evidence.reference_title: Fraser syndrome: epidemiological study in a European population.
evidence.snippet: Bilateral renal agenesis was present in 12/24 (50%) and unilateral in 4/24 (17%) cases.

nodes.description: Staged oculoplastic surgery - dissection of corneal adhesions, mucous membrane grafting, eyelid switch flaps and fornix reconstruction - aims to protect the cornea and optimize limited visual potential, mainly in abortive cryptophthalmos. Postoperative acuity is poor (perception of light to 20/200) in the largest reported series.

evidence.reference_title: A surgical strategy for the correction of Fraser syndrome cryptophthalmos.
evidence.snippet: Surgical steps included dissection of corneal adhesions from keratinized cornea, mucous membrane graft, Mustarde eyelid switch flap with subsequent division, and further lower lid augmentation as required (n = 10).

evidence.reference_title: A surgical strategy for the correction of Fraser syndrome cryptophthalmos.
evidence.snippet: Postoperative acuities ranged from perception of light to 20/200. Good outcomes in terms of corneal health were achieved in 6 of the 10 eyes operated on for incomplete cryptophthalmos.
